title: Perfect Chocolate Soufflé
description: A light, airy, and rich classic French dessert. Crisp on the outside with a warm, molten-like center.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar, plus more for coating ramekins
3 ounces (85g) high-quality bittersweet chocolate (60-70% cacao), chopped
2 tablespoons (30g) unsalted butter, plus more for greasing ramekins
3 large egg yolks, at room temperature
4 large egg whites, at room temperature
steps: Prep Ramekins: Butter four 6-ounce ramekins using upward brush strokes (this helps the soufflé rise straight). Coat the inside of each ramekin with granulated sugar, tapping out the excess. Place on a baking sheet and refrigerate.
Preheat Oven: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).

Melt Chocolate: Melt the chopped chocolate and 2 tablespoons of butter in a heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (double boiler). Stir until smooth, then remove from heat to cool slightly.

Make the Base (Roux & Pastry Cream): In a small saucepan over medium heat, melt another 1 tablespoon of butter. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and salt. Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil. Remove from heat and whisk into the melted chocolate mixture. Whisk in the egg yolks one at a time until smooth.

Whip Egg Whites: In a clean glass or metal bowl, beat the egg whites and cream of tartar on medium speed until soft peaks form. Gradually add the 1/2 cup of sugar one tablespoon at a time, increasing speed to high, until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Fold: Gently fold about 1/3 of the whipped egg whites into the chocolate base to lighten it. Fold in the remaining egg whites in two batches, being very gentle to avoid deflating the batter.

Bake: Divide the batter evenly among the prepared ramekins. Run your thumb around the inside rim of each ramekin to create a small gap (helps rising). Bake for 12-15 minutes until puffed and the centers jiggle slightly. Serve immediately!

title: Buttermilk Substitutes & Troubleshooting
description: Running low on buttermilk? Here are the best quick substitutions and baking tips for achieving that perfect acidity and moisture.
ingredients: For 1 cup of substitute: 1 cup milk (whole or 2%) OR 1 cup unsweetened soy milk
Acidifier: 1 tablespoon lemon juice OR 1 tablespoon white distilled vinegar
Alternative substitute: 3/4 cup plain yogurt + 1/4 cup water or milk
steps: Acidified Milk Method: Measure 1 tablespoon of lemon juice or white vinegar into a liquid measuring cup. Add enough milk to equal 1 cup total. Stir gently and let sit at room temperature for 5 to 10 minutes. The milk will curdle slightly and become acidic.
Yogurt Method: Whisk 3/4 cup of plain yogurt with 1/4 cup of water or milk until smooth. Use 1-to-1 in place of buttermilk.
Cream of Tartar Method: Whisk 1 and 1/2 teaspoons of cream of tartar into the dry ingredients of your recipe, then add 1 cup of regular milk with the wet ingredients.
Why it matters: Buttermilk adds acidity that activates baking soda (causing baked goods to rise) and tenderizes gluten, resulting in a soft crumb.

title: Classic Homemade Marinara Sauce
description: A simple, clean, and delicious Italian tomato sauce ready in under 45 minutes.
ingredients: 1 can (28 ounces) whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes
4 cloves garlic, peeled and thinly sliced
1 sprig fresh basil OR 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano
steps: Prep Tomatoes: Pour the canned tomatoes into a bowl and crush them by hand or with a fork to your desired consistency.

Sauté Garlic: In a medium saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium-low heat. Add the sliced garlic and red pepper flakes. Cook, stirring frequently, until the garlic is fragrant and lightly golden (do not burn, or it will taste bitter).

Simmer Sauce: Carefully pour the crushed tomatoes with their juices into the pan (watch out for splatters). Add salt and the basil sprig (or dried oregano). Bring to a simmer, then lower heat to maintain a gentle bubble.
Cook: Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and the oil has emulsified into the tomatoes. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve: Discard the basil sprig. Serve warm over pasta, as a dipping sauce, or as a base for pizza.
